scenes.title: LIMIT
scenes.narration: LIMIT caps how many rows a query returns, which is essential for previews and top-N lists.

scenes.title: Why limit rows
bullets: Pairs with ORDER BY for top results
scenes.narration: LIMIT restricts the number of rows in the result, so you receive only as many as you ask for. This makes exploratory queries fast because the database can stop early. Combined with ORDER BY, it becomes the standard way to fetch the top or bottom records.

scenes.title: Top five earners
scenes.code:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
ORDER BY salary DESC
LIMIT 5;
scenes.narration: First ORDER BY sorts every employee by salary from highest to lowest. LIMIT then keeps only the first five rows of that sorted list. The result is a clean top-five ranking of the best-paid employees.

scenes.title: Limit in the pipeline
steps: Apply LIMIT to keep top rows
scenes.narration: The query filters and selects its rows as usual, then sorts them with ORDER BY. LIMIT applies last, trimming the sorted output down to your requested count. Without a sort, the rows kept by LIMIT are effectively arbitrary.

scenes.text: Always pair LIMIT with ORDER BY when the specific rows matter, not just the count.
scenes.narration: Use LIMIT to cap results, and always add an ORDER BY when which rows you keep actually matters.
